headline: Economist Paul Krugman argues that the AI building boom is already pushing up borrowing costs and squeezing out investment in housing, offices and factories.
score_reason: Lowered from 5 because Krugman's post was published on 6 Oct, before the scan window; Benzinga's write-up came two days later.
importance_line: Homebuyers, builders and businesses outside AI would face higher borrowing costs if he is right, but it is one economist's argument, and he admits that forecasts of a bubble are only educated guesses.
source: Paul Krugman's Substack, as relayed by Benzinga
summary: Benzinga reports that economist Paul Krugman wrote in his Substack newsletter on Tuesday 6 Oct 2026 that spending on AI data centres is pushing up interest rates and "crowding out" other investment, which he says did not happen in the 1990s tech boom because foreign money then flowed into the US. Krugman calls this "not a hypothetical risk" because it is happening now, while saying forecasts of an AI bubble are "at best educated guesses".
notes: Pool source Yahoo Finance (Benzinga text); credited to Krugman's own post, which we read, with Benzinga as relay. Score lowered 1 for age.
